# `silk/trace/perfetto`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Perfetto trace encoding and decoding for recorder batches and counter samples.

A Perfetto trace is a sequence of `TracePacket` messages, each one written as field 1 of the
`Trace` message. Bytes made of whole packets are a trace on their own, and so is a file that
several writers append whole packets to. The Perfetto UI and `trace_processor` open it, with each
span as a slice on the track of the thread that opened it, each log as an instant on the
process's `log` track, and each metric series and counter sample as a counter track.
[`Perfetto`](#Perfetto) writes such a trace a batch at a time, and [`PerfettoReader`](#PerfettoReader) reads one back a
chunk at a time, so a reader can follow a file that a running program still appends to.

Import as `Perfetto` with `import silk.trace.perfetto { Perfetto }`.

Public declarations: 8.

<a id="Perfetto"></a>

## `Perfetto`

```silk
pub struct Perfetto
```

One process's Perfetto packet sequence: the names it has interned and the tracks it has
described.

### When to use
Keep one `Perfetto` for each process that writes a trace, and pass it every batch and sample
the process writes, so that each name and track is written once. As a [`Sink`](./trace-sink.md#Sink) it writes each
batch to the active `Writer`.

### Details
The process ID numbers the sequence, so the packets of processes that append to one file at
the same time keep their interned names apart. A span becomes a slice on the track of the
thread that opened it, or on the process's `spans` track when the target gives no thread ID,
with its attributes, source location and error as arguments, and its ID and its parent's as
`span.id` and `parent.id`. The trace a span belongs to is written as `trace.id.high` and
`trace.id.low` on the first span of each trace in a row, and holds for the spans after it in
the sequence, so a reader rebuilds every parent link and trace whatever thread or process a
parent ran on ([`PerfettoReader`](#PerfettoReader)). A log becomes an instant named by its template on the
process's `log` track, with its message, severity and the IDs of the span current when it was
written. Each metric series becomes a counter track named by its instrument and attributes; a
histogram has no single value over time and is left out. Times are the recorder's Unix
nanoseconds.

### Gotchas
A trace viewer nests slices by their times. Two spans of one thread that start at the same
nanosecond nest in the order they were written, which is the order they ended, so a span and
its first child must start at different times. The recorder's tick counters ensure it on Apple
and Linux targets, where opening a span takes longer than one tick.


Appends to `output` the value `value` of the counter `name` at `time`, in Unix nanoseconds,

<a id="PerfettoReader"></a>

## `PerfettoReader`

```silk
pub struct PerfettoReader
```

Decodes a Perfetto trace into [`Event`](#Event)s, a chunk of bytes at a time.

### When to use
Read a trace that [`Perfetto`](#Perfetto) or another TrackEvent writer recorded: a whole file at once,
or a file a running program still appends to, by passing each newly appended chunk to
[`read`](#PerfettoReader.impl.read) with whatever the last call left unread before it.

### Details
A packet's interned names stay with its sequence until the sequence says its state was
cleared, so a reader must see a sequence from its first packet. [`Perfetto`](#Perfetto) writes each span's
start and end side by side, and the reader joins them into one [`Event.Slice`](#Event.Slice); it holds a
start until the next packet shows whether its end follows, and [`finish`](#PerfettoReader.impl.finish) hands over the last
one. A span's trace comes from the latest `trace.id` fields of its sequence. Packet timestamps
are read as they are: a trace that times packets by clock snapshots or timestamp deltas reads
with the raw values.

<a id="PerfettoReader.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make() -> Self
```

A reader at the start of a trace.

<a id="PerfettoReader.impl.read"></a>

### Method `read`

```silk
pub effect fn read(self: &mut Self, bytes: &[u8], events: &mut List<Event>) -> usize
    ! PerfettoError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Decodes the whole packets at the start of `bytes`, appends their events to `events`, and
returns how many bytes it decoded. A packet that `bytes` ends inside is left unread: pass its
bytes again, with what follows them, to the next call.

#### Errors
- [`PerfettoError`](#PerfettoError) for bytes that are not a Perfetto trace, at the packet at fault; the
  events of the packets before it are appended.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot hold the events or the interned names.

<a id="PerfettoReader.impl.finish"></a>

### Method `finish`

```silk
pub effect fn finish(self: &mut Self, events: &mut List<Event>) -> () ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Hands over, as an [`Event.Begin`](#Event.Begin), the slice start the last packet left waiting for its end.
Call it once no more bytes of the trace will come.
